involve immediate human safety, unlike abstract evolutionary models."],"overturn_conditions":["If a formal link can be established between severity of test and increased logical probability of the optimization."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_003","SRC_012"],"transfer_claims":["Just as we bet on the fittest organism without guaranteeing its survival, we bet on the best-corroborated theory without his own terms as a non-inductive 'critical preference' grounded in the logic of testing rather than probability, but accepting this costs the agent any rational assurance that the preferred theory between 'inductive inference' (claiming past success increases future probability) and 'critical preference' (choosing the theory that has withstood the most severe attempts at falsification as the best available target for further criticism and action). Preference is justified not because the theory is likely true, but because it is the most informative and rigorously tested survivor, making it the rational choice for a fallibilist who must act despite lacking certainty. The cost is the abandonment of the hope that rationality guarantees practical success; one acts on the best-tested theory knowing it may still fail tomorrow, as corroboration reports only on past performance, not future reliability.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
